records.name: Apurímac
records.current_summary: No documented sub-national signal for Apurímac: the country dossier lists this department among the regions where no region-specific trans law, ordinance, incident series or enforcement finding could be located, and all three attached sources are national in scope. What binds Apurímac is the national frame: a congressional bill package (6506/8457, committee-approved February 2025) would bar trans people from public sanitary facilities of the opposite sex at birth, and national data record 54 killings and 170 rights-violation cases of TLGBI people between 2020 and 2023 with trans women most affected and hate crimes rising - no regional deviation documented either way.

sources.claim: Infobae Perú (20 Feb 2025) reports the congressional Women and Family Commission unanimously approved a draft opinion (dictamen) merging bills 6506 and 8457, introduced by congressmen Jorge Montoya and Alejandro Muñante, barring trans people from public restrooms that do not correspond to their birth sex, with exceptions for custody, where medical attention is required, or accompanying an elderly person, a child under 12 or a person with disabilities, plus a ban on 'ambiguous' bathroom signage; the trigger was a July 2023 social-media complaint over the Jorge Chávez airport's gendered restroom labels. LGTBIQ activist Gianna Camacho calls the measure discriminatory, warning that bathroom access would come to depend on security staff's personal judgment (including ID checks), and notes there is no record of sexual assault by trans women in women's restrooms. It contains no Apurímac-specific legal, enforcement or incident finding; for this record its value is the national ban on gender-matching restroom access that binds the region (committee stage, February 2025).

IDEHPUCP legal analysis by Miriam Tovar and Gonzalo Ugarte (15 Apr 2025) confirms that on Wednesday 2 April 2025 the congressional Plenary approved and exempted from second vote a bill whose article 5 bars any person from entering or using a public sanitary service that does not correspond to their 'biological sex', save for narrow listed exceptions, and argues this directly violates the equal-treatment and non-discrimination principle of article 2(2) of the Peruvian Constitution and article 1.1 of the American Convention on Human Rights. The authors say the law's stated aim of preventing child sexual abuse rests on a stigmatising stereotype implicitly presenting trans people as likely restroom harassers, while UN reporting shows trans people are more often victims than aggressors. It contains no Apurímac-specific finding; for this record its value is the human-rights institute's analysis of the national framework that governs the region.

Agencia Presentes (22 Jul 2024), covering the Observatorio de Derechos TLGBI annual report, records 54 murders of TLGBI people and 170 rights-violation cases in Peru over 2020-2023, with trans women more than half the homicide victims (30), followed by 23 gay men and one lesbian; killings rose to 19 in 2023 (12 trans women) from 13 in 2022, 10 in 2021 and 12 in 2020, many committed with cruelty (multiple gunshots, stabbings), and the 170 violation cases include state violence and incitement to discrimination (61 denuncias in 2020). It recounts the February 2023 gang abduction of trans sex worker Rubí Torres Silvano, 31, in central Lima and her killing in Carabayllo with about 30 gunshots as part of an extortion scheme. It contains no Apurímac-specific finding; for this record its value is the national hate-violence data the regional assessment relies on.

freshness_all.fact: Peru enacted Law 32331 on 13 May 2025 barring trans people from public restrooms matching gender identity; the 2024 congressional-movement piece is superseded by the enacted law. N

records.name: Arequipa
records.current_summary: No documented sub-national signal for Arequipa: the country dossier lists this department among the regions where no region-specific trans law, ordinance, incident series or enforcement finding could be located, and all three attached sources are national in scope. What binds Arequipa is the national frame: a congressional bill package (6506/8457, committee-approved February 2025) would bar trans people from public sanitary facilities of the opposite sex at birth, and national data record 54 killings and 170 rights-violation cases of TLGBI people between 2020 and 2023 with trans women most affected and hate crimes rising - no regional deviation documented either way.

sources.claim: Infobae Perú (20 Feb 2025) reports the Congress' Commission on Women and Family unanimously approved a dictamen covering bills 6506 and 8457 that would bar entry to public sanitary facilities destined to the sex opposite to one's birth sex — exceptions only for custody, medical care, or accompanying an adult, a child under 12 or a disabled person — and require unambiguous signage; as of publication it still awaited plenary backing. Trans-rights activist Gianna Camacho is quoted calling the measure discriminatory, warning that security staff would effectively judge people by personal criteria (e.g. requesting their DNI). No Arequipa-specific provision appears; the source supports this record's claim that the national rule binds the department.

IDEHPUCP analysis by Miriam Tovar and Gonzalo Ugarte (15 Apr 2025) reports the Congress plenary on 2 April 2025 approved, exempt from second vote, the dictamen of the law 'fortaleciendo el derecho a la indemnidad sexual de los niños y adolescentes', whose article 5 bars anyone whose biological sex does not match the facility's intended sex from public sanitary facilities, with exceptions limited to accompanying/assisting minors, patients or people with specific needs. The authors argue the measure implicitly brands trans people as more prone to entering bathrooms to harass or sexually abuse minors, conditions basic rights on verifiable 'biological sex', and violates equality, non-discrimination and gender self-determination; they note Congress had already banned inclusive language and again rejected equal marriage. No Arequipa-specific finding appears; the source supports this record's critique claim.

Agencia Presentes (22 Jul 2024) reports the TLGBI Rights Observatory's annual report: 54 killings of TLGBI people and 170 rights-violation cases in Peru between 2020 and 2023, trans women the most affected and hate crimes rising; it recounts the February 2023 kidnapping of trans woman Rubí Torres Silvano (31) in central Lima and her murder in Carabayllo with approximately 30 gunshots at the hands of the 'Los Gallegos' gang, with bodies showing gunshots, stab wounds and throat-slitting indicating extreme hate. No Arequipa-specific finding appears; the national data frame the risk environment this record claims applies to the department.

records.name: Moquegua
records.current_summary:
Moquegua has no recorded trans-specific regional law, ordinance or enforcement finding, and the available sources are all national. The congressional committee on women and family unanimously approved the report backing bills 6506 and 8457, which would bar trans people from public sanitary facilities designated for the sex opposite their birth sex — exceptions only for custody, medical care and accompanying children under 12, the elderly or disabled — and require unambiguous signage; as of February 2025 the report still awaited full-chamber approval. An academic human-rights bulletin critiques the measure as implicitly branding trans people a sexual risk to minors, part of the institute's coverage of legalised discrimination.

Moquegua itself shows no documented deviation in either direction.

records.name: Adana
records.current_summary:
This province has no province-specific law, ordinance or incident series in the audited record; what a trans visitor here stands under is the same national framework that binds every province. A leaked draft omnibus justice package from October 2025 (the '11th Judicial Package') would enable criminal charges against LGBT people across Turkiye - Human Rights Watch called it one of the most alarming rights rollbacks in decades - and it contains no province-specific provisions. The LGBTI+ association Kaos GL reported that in 2025 anti-LGBTI+ hostility became institutionalised as state policy under a 'Year of the Family' banner, with senior officials' rhetoric and instructions to public institutions creating a climate encouraging rights violations.

Because the surviving record is entirely national-level and carries no provincial breakdown, neither a more protective nor a more hostile local regime can be established for this province; the documented national picture applies here unchanged.

sources.claim: Human Rights Watch article (29 Oct 2025): a leaked draft omnibus justice reform ('11th Judicial Package') would enable criminal charges against LGBT people in Türkiye — described by HRW as one of the most alarming rollbacks of rights in decades; Istanbul activists held a press conference against it (28 Oct 2025). National-level: applies countrywide if adopted, no province-specific provisions.

sources.title: LGBTQ rights in Turkey - Wikipedia
sources.claim: Wikipedia's Turkey country overview states the national framework every visitor to Adana Province stands under: same-sex sexual activity has been legal since 1858 (Ottoman penal code) and transgender people have been able to change their legal gender since 1988, when gender reassignment surgery became legal; Turkey has no comprehensive law prohibiting discrimination based on sexual orientation or gender identity, and LGBTQ people are barred from serving openly in the military; same-sex relationships receive no legal recognition - marriage, civil unions and domestic partnerships are unavailable - and same-sex couples cannot adopt jointly or as individuals. The page carries no Adana-specific content, so it supplies only the countrywide baseline against which the record's 'no province-specific regime' assessment sits.

records.name: Afyonkarahisar
records.current_summary:
This province has no province-specific law, ordinance or incident series in the audited record; what a trans visitor here stands under is the same national framework that binds every province. A leaked draft omnibus justice package from October 2025 (the '11th Judicial Package') would enable criminal charges against LGBT people across Turkiye - Human Rights Watch called it one of the most alarming rights rollbacks in decades - and it contains no province-specific provisions. The LGBTI+ association Kaos GL reported that in 2025 anti-LGBTI+ hostility became institutionalised as state policy under a 'Year of the Family' banner, with senior officials' rhetoric and instructions to public institutions creating a climate encouraging rights violations.

Because the surviving record is entirely national-level and carries no provincial breakdown, neither a more protective nor a more hostile local regime can be established for this province; the documented national picture applies here unchanged.

A 2026 recheck confirms the national crackdown pattern is still current: public LGBTI+ assembly remains banned and prosecuted, with no provincial reversal found.

sources.claim: Human Rights Watch (29 Oct 2025) reports a leaked draft of Türkiye's omnibus '11th Judicial Package' that would open the way to criminal charges against LGBT people — called one of the most alarming rollbacks of rights in decades: conduct deemed 'contrary to biological sex and general morality' including its so-called 'promotion' would bring up to three years in prison, participation in same-sex engagement or marriage ceremonies up to four years (same-sex marriage is not legal, so such ceremonies are by definition symbolic), and gender-affirming care would be restricted (surgery age raised from 18 to 25, mandatory permanent infertility), with medical professionals fined or imprisoned up to seven years and transgender patients up to three years for care outside the new limits, forcing treatment into underground settings. It contains no Afyonkarahisar-specific provision; the source supports this record's claim that this national framework is what a visitor stands under in the province.

Kaos GL's report on 2025 ('A Major Siege against LGBTI+ People in 2025: Hostility Turned into State Policy') documents six right-to-life violations, three recorded as hate-motivated killings with trans people the most affected (counted from media and civil-society reports because the state keeps no official hate-crime statistics), 89 torture or ill-treatment violations (up from 51), mostly linked to peaceful assembly, and 336 assembly and 313 liberty violations — a roughly 2.5-fold liberty increase mostly of detentions — with event-specific bans and violent police attacks on peaceful gatherings. It reports hostility institutionalised under 'Year of the Family' instructions to public institutions, hate speech from senior officials, censored broadcasts and cancelled artistic events, presented as national practice rather than provincial choice. No Afyonkarahisar-specific finding appears; the source supports this record's claims about the country-wide framework.

freshness_all.fact: Same basis as Adiyaman: 2025 siege report current; authorities still ban Pride and prosecute assembly; no provincial reversal found.
